content.text: Vedic Age: Early & Later Vedic Polity, Economy, Society & Literature

The Vedic Age (c. 1500–600 BCE) marked the pastoral-tribal settlement of Indo-Aryan communities in the Sapta Sindhu region and their subsequent eastward migration into the Ganga-Yamuna Doab. The advent of iron metallurgy ('Shyama Ayas') in the Later Vedic era catalyzed agrarian surpluses, territorial statehood (Janapadas), rigid four-fold Varna stratification, and complex sacrificial rituals.

content.caption: A 19th-century Devanagari manuscript of the Rigveda, preserving hymns composed in the Sapta Sindhu river basin.
Evolutionary Paradigm: Early Vedic (Rigvedic) vs Later Vedic Era
rows: Sapta Sindhu (Indus, Saraswati, Ravi, Beas, Chenab, Jhelum, Sutlej).
Aryavarta / Kuru-Panchala realm in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab.
Tribal chiefdom (Rajan) checked by popular assemblies (Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha); voluntary tributes (Bali).
Territorial monarchies (Janapadas); divine kingship; standing royal bureaucracy (Ratnins); compulsory taxation (Bali, Bhaga, Shulka).
Pastoral economy; cattle as primary wealth (Gavisti = search for cows); barter; copper/bronze (Ayas).
Sedentary iron-axe agriculture (Shyama Ayas); Painted Grey Ware (PGW); emergence of trade guilds (Srenis).
Flexible occupational classes; absence of hereditary caste; women enjoyed high status (Gargi, Maitreyi).
Rigid hereditary four-fold Varna (Purusha Sukta); Gotra endogamy; exclusion of women from political assemblies and education.
Polytheistic nature deities (Indra/Purandara, Agni, Varuna); simple fire oblations without large-scale killings.
Ascendancy of Trimurti/Prajapati, Rudra, and Vishnu; costly animal sacrifices (Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya); Upanishadic philosophical revolt.

items: Vedic Literary Corpus: Shruti (revealed: 4 Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads) and Smriti (remembered: Vedangas, Upavedas, Dharmashastras, Epics).

Four Vedas: Rigveda (1,028 suktas, Gayatri Mantra in Mandala 3); Samaveda (book of melodies, origins of Indian classical music); Yajurveda (prose ritual formulas: Shukla and Krishna); Atharvaveda (charms, spells, medicine, daily customs).

Upanishadic Philosophy: 108 Upanishads (principal 10: Isha, Kena, Katha, Mundaka, Chandogya, Brihadaranyaka); central thesis of Moksha through realizing the identity of Atman (individual soul) and Brahman (universal consciousness).
Six Vedangas: Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhanda (metrics), and Jyotisha (astronomy).

content.text: Part A: Mains Analytical & Descriptive Questions

items:
Trace the socio-economic and political shifts from the Early Vedic pastoral tribalism to the Later Vedic territorial statehood. How did iron technology facilitate this structural transition? (APPSC Group-1 Mains, 10 Marks)
-> Model Approach: Contrast the Sapta Sindhu pastoralism with Ganga-Yamuna agricultural settlements; explain the metallurgical revolution of iron ('Shyama Ayas') from 1000 BCE at Atranjikhera clearing dense monsoonal sal forests; examine the rise of surplus paddy cultivation yielding land revenue that financed royal armies and ritual legitimacy (Rajasuya, Vajapeya); evaluate the hardening of Varna hierarchies and social subjugation of Shudras and women.

content.text: Part B: Screening / Prelims Objective Questions

items:
Q1. Which famous Vedic assembly was open to women and functioned as the earliest popular deliberative tribal council in the Early Vedic era?
(a) Sabha
(b) Samiti
(c) Vidatha
(d) Gana
Correct Answer: (c) Vidatha [Explanation: The Vidatha was the earliest Rigvedic folk assembly where women actively participated alongside men in tribal deliberations, religious rites, and war loot distribution.]

Q2. The national motto of India, 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth Alone Triumphs), is inscribed from which ancient Upanishad?
(a) Chandogya Upanishad
(b) Mundaka Upanishad
(c) Katha Upanishad
(d) Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
Correct Answer: (b) Mundaka Upanishad [Explanation: 'Satyameva Jayate' is an excerpt from the Mundaka Upanishad (3.1.6), adopted as the official national motto on 26 January 1950.]

Q3. In the Later Vedic administrative apparatus, which royal functionary among the Ratnins was designated as the Chief Collector of Revenue?
(a) Suta
(b) Bhagadugha
(c) Sangrahitri
(d) Akshavapa
Correct Answer: (b) Bhagadugha [Explanation: In the Later Vedic state, the Bhagadugha collected the king's share of agrarian taxes (Bhaga), while the Sangrahitri functioned as the royal treasurer.]

Q4. The philosophical dialogue between the young seeker Nachiketa and Yama (the God of Death) regarding the nature of the soul and life after death is preserved in:
(a) Katha Upanishad
(b) Kena Upanishad
(c) Prashna Upanishad
(d) Aitareya Upanishad
Correct Answer: (a) Katha Upanishad [Explanation: The famous discourse on self-realization, the immortality of Atman, and spiritual wisdom between Yama and Nachiketa is the central subject of the Katha Upanishad.]

Q5. Which Mandala of the Rigveda contains the famous 'Purusha Sukta' hymn that provides the earliest textual reference to the four-fold Varna system?
(a) Mandala 1
(b) Mandala 3
(c) Mandala 7
(d) Mandala 10
Correct Answer: (d) Mandala 10 [Explanation: Mandala 10, Hymn 90 (Purusha Sukta) represents a late Rigvedic interpolation describing the cosmic sacrifice of Purusha from whose mouth, arms, thighs, and feet the Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra arose.]
